grades.quote: All floating-point operations that perform rounding can select the rounding mode using the _rm_ field with the encoding shown in Table 25.
grades.reason: Explains instruction-specific selection through rm, but not its relationship to frm.

grades.quote:
||Source Registers|Destination Registers|Accumulating CSRs||
|---|---|---|---|---|
|FMSUB.S|rs1, rs2, rs3, frm*|rd|NV, OF, UF, NX|*if rm=111|
grades.reason: Shows that frm is read when rm=111, but does not explain the rounding modes or other rm encodings.

grades.quote:
|Number|Privilege|Name|Description|
|---|---|---|---|
|||Floating-Point|Control and Status Registers|
|0x001|Read write|fflags|Floating-Point Accrued Exceptions.|
|0x002|Read write|frm|Floating-Point Dynamic Rounding Mode.|
grades.reason: Identifies frm as the dynamic rounding-mode CSR, without explaining selection through rm.

grades.quote: As with other scalar floating-point instructions, the rounding mode field `rm` can also take on the `DYN` encoding, which indicates that the instruction uses the rounding mode specified in the `frm` CSR.
grades.reason: Explains direct rm rounding-mode encodings and dynamic selection of frm through rm=111.
